analysis.title: JPM US Market Intelligence Morning Briefing (October 26, 2026)
key_insights: JPM Market Intel remains Tactically Bullish. SPX is down 2.4% over two weeks, but the desk expects growth at or above trend (flash PMIs imply ~5% annualized real growth) and positive earnings growth to support stocks. The signal is less clear because positioning has not fully washed out even though sentiment is in Fear.
Upcoming macro: the Fed, ECB and BOJ all meet this week and all three are expected to deliver hawkish pauses. Mag7 earnings resume Wednesday.

Pre-market: futures are higher with Semis and Memory leading Tech. Brazil's surprise election result has EWZ down 27% pre-market. WTI is down 243bp at $100.76, gold is near $4,016 and the 10Y yield is 4.990%.

APAC client trip: APAC clients are more bearish than US clients but less bearish than European clients. Many are still up double digits on the year and lack incentive to re-engage until a clear trend emerges.

US consumer: the desk sees little evidence of a K-shaped economy or consumer cracks. The top four income quintiles hold 6% to 27% more real cash than at YE2019 (nearly $8T nominal). Retail sales run $723bn a month YTD2026 vs $505bn in 2019. Card delinquencies and charge-offs are normalizing to pre-COVID trends, not deteriorating.
Corporate health: HY default rate is 2.7% vs a 3.2% long-term average, and SPX is near all-time highs with record-level margins.

Consumer sub-sectors: Airlines, Cruise and Hotels show robust demand. Autos and Homebuilders face affordability limits, so parts and suppliers may be a better expression. Retailers face freight costs (30-40% of total cost) that have more than tripled YTD. Restaurants lack conviction. Staples are the most at risk of margin compression and likely a source of funds.

AI credit: JPM credit research sees markets becoming more discriminating on AI infrastructure but no broader funding crisis. AI infrastructure has absorbed over $500bn of debt YTD. Hyperscaler all-in funding costs are up ~120bp. Leveraged GPU and data center developers face tighter terms, and power availability is seen as the main constraint on buildout.

AI-related CDS spreads are wide on technical selling and bank hedging of data center lending exposure, pushing CDS above comparable cash bonds. The desk sees selling protection on positive-basis names as attractive. CRWV has converts outstanding and CDS at a slightly positive basis.

CRWV is seen as a financing challenge, not a solvency one. JPM credit analyst Tom Egan projects last-12-month EBITDA rising from ~$4.4b in June 2026 to $7.3b by YE and nearly $20b by YE27, with ~$130b of contracted revenue. ORCL and SpaceX spreads widened on reports of off-balance-sheet financing. Nvidia is flagged as a transmission channel for financial stress through its GPU customers.

France/Europe: the desk calls contagion fears exaggerated and sees a French idiosyncratic story, not a sovereign crisis 2.0. OATs discount debt/GDP above 150% (vs ~120% actual) and an implied deficit above 8% (vs ~5% debated). No material reversal is expected before 2Q27 elections, but relief is possible into year-end around the budget. EU Banks dips of more than 15% vs the index should be bought, and call ratio spreads and call spreads are attractive.

Midterms: federal AI regulation is unlikely because Trump would veto and Democrats cannot reach a two-thirds override. A Democratic House could defund Middle East military efforts, forcing an off-ramp. Tariff policy is unlikely to change. Longer-dated bonds could see a bid if Democrats halt deficit spending. Markets see a Blue Wave as most likely.

Treasuries: before the Oct 22 rally the view was that a 10Y yield of 5.50% was more likely than 5.00%. The market prices a hike in Dec 2026 and two more in FY27. Downside risk to that path is a quick end to the US/Iran conflict and normalization of oil. JPM's Jay Barry says 10Y yields are 15bp too low on his fair-value framework and risks skew modestly higher.

Rates desk (Ryan Ward) explains the bond market's resilience through four forces: the AI wobble, French stress and global relative value, a long-end short-covering unwind (falling open interest in WN and US futures), and a Treasury primary dealer agenda read as probing a cut to long-end coupon supply.

Trade feedback: no high-conviction ideas, and discussions were split between AI and non-AI. Pushbacks on AI bulls include supply-constrained Semis pricing and Neocloud turmoil and bankruptcy risk (hyperscalers likely buy assets cheaply). Software is no longer a funding short. The desk's buy trigger is a positioning flush, hyperscaler capex confirmation, Semis earnings, tighter credit and seasonality, pointing to early November.

Breadth: since the July 28 lows SPX is +4.8%, but 69% of stocks lag the index, which makes single-stock picks hedged with sector ETFs hard. Clients see many businesses as built for a lower-rate world (10Y averaged 2.39% in the 2010s vs 3.14% this decade).

Funding shorts for Tech exposure: clients mentioned Consumer, Healthcare, Smidcaps and Europe. Other assets: the dollar is seen range-bound with a likely local high, gold trades inversely to the dollar, none see credit as superior to equities, copper bull case is intact, and silver is treated as an AI proxy.

Monetization Menu: the prior (Oct 19) menu stays, favoring Tech through pairs and derivatives, Financials and Retailers, and Brazil and Japan. The desk would add hedges via longs in oil/Energy equities and long vol.

Iran: Trump is nearing a decision between negotiation and continued attacks as a third carrier approaches. If he returns to negotiations, the desk expects a broad rally led by Tech and Cyclicals ex-Energy. Clients expect another wave of attacks after US and Israeli elections, with the risk that Iran targets regional energy infrastructure.

Earnings season: with 24% of SPX reported, blended revenue growth is 12.7% and EPS growth is 29.5%, with no dip vs pre-season expectations and margins of 14.9%. Q4 is expected at 13.0% revenue and 29.2% EPS growth. FY26 is expected at 12.5% revenue and 33.1% EPS growth, and FY27 at 9.5% and 16.0%.

Earnings read-through: consumer strength shows up across SYF, PG, UNP, AXP and COF (domestic card charge-offs 3.98%, down 65bp YoY). MMM raised its oil inflation estimate to $185m from $150-175m and expects to offset it with pricing. PG warned oil above $110 is an increasing headwind. Companies are passing through energy and tariff costs, so inflation pressure stays sticky.

FOMC preview (Feroli): he expects a hold with two hawkish dissents from Hammack and Logan, and a risk that Kashkari also dissents. Chair Warsh must explain why the Committee hiked after a two-tenths September core PCE but holds on an expected three-tenths. The Committee is biased to hike but wants more time to observe the effect of last month's hike.

Positioning Intelligence: hedge funds are -3.3% MTD globally while SPX is +0.2% MTD, and Eq L/S 20d alpha of -2.9% is the worst since Feb '21. Selling was moderate for HFs, steadier from CTAs (US equity exposure down every day since 10/13). The desk reads it as systematic de-risking, not a liquidation. Net leverage is at 12m and 3yr lows but gross leverage is still above average, so positioning has not fully cleared.

Flows: combined ETF, retail and HF 60d relative flows into Info Tech are near record highs (+3z), while Utilities (60d -2.5z), Real Estate (20d -4.9z) and Materials (60d -2.7z) are at or near extreme lows. Healthcare is the defensive exception (20d +2.8z).
The Recession L/S basket returned 3.4% and the Stagflation L/S basket 1.5% last week, even though 1Y and 2Y breakevens fell and oil rose for a 4th straight week.

market_movers.rationale: Brazil's surprise election result has EWZ down 27% pre-market. The desk had previously favored Brazil internationally.
JPM credit sees a financing challenge, not solvency, with EBITDA projected near $20b by YE27 and ~$130b contracted revenue. CDS trades at a slightly positive basis.
Credit spreads widened significantly on reports of off-balance-sheet financing, and more externally financed names have underperformed.

sector_views.rationale: Revenue and earnings growth differential points to Tech domination once the market stabilizes, and the desk retains a preference for Tech through pairs and derivatives.
Constructive on consumer resilience and limited direct AI exposure. Clients focus on GSIBs and credit cards.
Favored on consumer resilience, though freight costs of 30-40% of total cost, up more than 3x YTD, are a headwind for some clients.
Seen as most at risk of margin compression and a likely source of funds with higher rates and inflation.
Clients see negative outlook if a Blue Wave halts a military funding spike, though a lame-duck military funding bill could surprise to the upside.
Increasingly a long play rather than a funding short, with security and infrastructure software as consensus longs.
Earnings trend unchanged. Dips of more than 15% vs the index should be bought, and call ratio spreads and call spreads are attractive.

earnings_insights: FactSet blended Q3 SPX with 24% reported: revenue growth 12.7% and EPS growth 29.5% (actual plus forecast), vs pre-season expectations of 12.7% and 29.5%, with 14.9% margins.

Reference: Q2 2026 was 15.6% revenue growth, 52.3% EPS growth and 17% margins. Q4 2026 estimate is 13.0% revenue and 29.2% EPS growth. FY26 estimate is 12.5% revenue and 33.1% EPS growth. FY27 estimate is 9.5% revenue and 16.0% EPS growth.
COF reported Q3 domestic card charge-off rate of 3.98%, down 73bp QoQ and 65bp YoY.
MMM raised its oil cost inflation estimate to $185 million from $150-175 million given in July, plus about $280 million of tariffs, and said pricing fully offsets it.
PG management said that if oil stays north of $110 it will be an increasing headwind for the year.
About 65% of SPX companies mentioned AI operational improvement in Q2 2026 earnings, but fewer than 5% quantified the impact.

Earnings this week: VZ reports BMO Oct 26. MSFT and GOOGL report AMC Oct 28. AMZN, INTC and COIN report AMC Oct 29. KO, PYPL, V, BA report Oct 27. CAT, LLY, MA report Oct 29. XOM and CVX report Oct 30.

The Committee hiked after this print, which Warsh must reconcile with a hold on an expected three-tenths.
Expected outturn that Feroli says makes the hold harder to explain after the September hike.
Second consecutive month pointing to ~5% real growth with building inflation pressure. S&P's chief economist forecast Q3 GDP at 4%.
Yield fell 7.8bp last week. Jay Barry sees it 15bp too low on a fair-value framework, with risks skewing higher.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Clients see upside risk to this path. The Fed dots show no hikes in FY27, which many see as not tied to high-probability outcomes.

trade_ideas.description: Add hedges via longs in oil and Energy equities and long vol to the Tactically Bullish stance (Monetization Menu).
trade_ideas.rationale: The prior menu aligns with the view and the Iran headline risk is a key tail risk.

trade_ideas.description: Buy EU Banks on dips of more than 15% vs the index, and use call ratio spreads and call spreads.
trade_ideas.rationale: Earnings trend for EU Banks is unchanged and the backdrop is attractive for call structures.
trade_ideas.risk: A sovereign crisis style escalation in France or EGB spreads.

trade_ideas.description: Sell AI-related CDS protection on names trading positive basis (CRWV highlighted), posting only initial margin.
trade_ideas.rationale: CDS trades above cash-bond spreads because of bank hedging demand rather than deteriorating fundamentals.
trade_ideas.risk: Growing debt supply and CRWV financing stress.

trade_ideas.description: Prefer Tech exposure through pairs trades and derivatives, with Financials and Retailers in Cyclicals, and Brazil and Japan internationally (Oct 19 menu).
trade_ideas.rationale: Selective expression of the bullish view after last week's sell-off, given consumer resilience and limited direct AI exposure.
trade_ideas.risk: Brazil is now exposed to the surprise election result.

trade_ideas.description: Fund Tech longs with shorts in a combination of Consumer, Healthcare, Smidcaps and Europe.
trade_ideas.rationale: Tech's size requires multiple sectors or geographies to offset.

trade_ideas.description: Play Autos and Homebuilders through parts and suppliers rather than the end names.
trade_ideas.rationale: Rates-sensitive sectors with affordability issues, car average age over 10 years and homes ~45 years.

risk_factors: Iran escalation, including strikes on regional energy infrastructure with global spare capacity and SPRs at limits.
Hawkish Fed surprises, more dissents and an unclear press conference from Chair Warsh, with Fed-induced volatility possibly extending into next week.
AI infrastructure financing: growing debt issuance, interconnected financing, higher borrowing cost, and delivery of compute capacity on schedule. Neocloud bankruptcy risk.
French fiscal slippage and political instability spreading to EGB spreads and EU banks.
Incomplete positioning washout, with CTAs still able to sell, soft retail demand and deteriorating Eq L/S alpha.
Sticky inflation as companies pass through energy and tariff costs, and 10Y yields below fair value.
Treasury supply changes (possible cut in long-end coupon supply) flattening the curve and widening bond spreads.
Midterms on Nov 3 and trade truce expiry on Nov 1.
charts_described: Marketing trip charts section lists SPX EPS growth vs nominal and real GDP, ISM Services prices paid vs headline CPI, total cash pile by income percentile (YE19 = 100, inflation-adjusted), household debt payments as a percentage of disposable income, OAT vs other EGB spreads, JPM positioning intel on Semis, and SPX stocks with negative beta. The text gives no chart values beyond those quoted elsewhere.
vol_and_positioning: VIX at 19.23. The desk's Monetization Menu suggests adding long vol as a hedge alongside oil and Energy equities.

Hedge funds are -3.3% MTD globally (YTD +4.7%, down from +6%). Eq L/S 20d alpha of -2.9% is the worst since Feb '21, and Multi-Strat alpha is the worst since Aug '24. 60d crowding returns of -4.1% are back to July '24 levels.

HF net flows were -0.9z (gross -0.6z). Multi-Strat 5d de-grossing slowed to -0.9% from -3.3%, and Quants kept adding gross (80th percentile). CTA US equity exposure fell every day since 10/13, led by Nasdaq, and sits only around the 45th percentile LT, so CTAs could still sell. Retail was a net buyer at the slowest pace in a year (5th percentile on 20d).

Eq L/S net leverage is at 12m and 3yr lows but gross leverage remains at the 77th percentile (12m) and 95th (5yr). AI Core Revenue and Semis positioning fell to the 94th percentile LT from the 99th. US TPM is at the 28th percentile, Europe the 8th.
Long-end Treasury futures open interest (WN and US) dropped, consistent with stop-outs and short covering that can flatten the curve.
French equities (both Exporters and Domestics) are shorted, making France a funder at the country level. OAT weakness was worsened by hedge fund crowding in carry proxies.
AI-related CDS trades wide of cash bonds because banks are buying protection to hedge data center lending exposure.
geopolitical: US/Iran conflict: Trump is deciding between negotiation and continued attacks as a third carrier nears the region. Iran has threatened to target the region including Israel and the UAE if bombing resumes.
Clients expect another wave of attacks after US and Israeli elections, with the risk of Iranian strikes on regional energy infrastructure while global spare capacity such as SPRs is at limits.
Brazil presidential runoff produced a surprise result that sent EWZ down 27% pre-market.
France fiscal and political instability driving OAT spread widening and EU bank weakness.
Trump-Xi one-year trade truce expires Nov 1, with a reported extension through January 20, 2027.
Israel legislative election Oct 27. US midterms Nov 3. US-Canada trade talks described by Hassett as 'very close' to a deal.

tension_points.bull_case: Hyperscalers are fundamentally well positioned, capital remains available (HY compute index +372bps YTD), and AI CDS wide of cash bonds offers attractive carry for protection sellers.
tension_points.bear_case: Leveraged GPU and data center developers face tighter financing, growing debt supply may pressure spreads into 2027, and Nvidia-linked circular financing introduces concentration risk.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Hyperscaler capex confirmation failing to arrive or credit spreads failing to tighten by early November.

tension_points.bull_case: Short term, AI and ex-AI can rally together, with cyclicals supported by strong PMIs and a flatter curve.
tension_points.bear_case: Longer term, revenue and earnings differentials point to Tech domination, and higher rates favor Quality, so only 31% of stocks beat the index since July.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A return to US/Iran negotiations would drive a broad rally led by Tech and Cyclicals ex-Energy, while renewed strikes would hurt the bull case.

tension_points.bull_case: Upside yield risk: strong balance sheets, accelerating growth and inflation, with the 10Y 15bp too low on fair value.
tension_points.bear_case: Fewer hikes if the US/Iran conflict ends and oil normalizes, plus safe-haven demand from OAT and AI stress.

tension_points.bull_case: France is idiosyncratic. Debt/GDP at ~120% is far from the 180% threshold, and the ECB backstop (TPI, OMT) limits disorderly widening.
tension_points.bear_case: The tape echoes the 2011-12 sovereign crisis with wider EGB spreads and lower EUR and EU Banks, and about 60% of French debt is held by non-residents.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Elections in 2Q27 are the point where the desk would reassess a material reversal.

theme_stances.key_argument: An economy growing at or above trend with positive earnings growth produces a bull market, and a refocus on fundamentals over AI fears should support stocks.
Credit markets are becoming more discriminating on AI infrastructure but there is nothing to suggest a broader funding crisis.
theme_stances.evidence: nothing to suggest a broader funding crisis

theme_stances.key_argument: Concerns that France is a leading indicator of EU-wide distress are exaggerated, since debt/GDP is far from the 180% threshold and the ECB backstop limits disorderly widening.
theme_stances.evidence: In our view, these concerns are exaggerated.
